name: Hallux Varus-Preaxial Polysyndactyly Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of hallux varus deformity characterized by medial deviation of the great toe
Preaxial polysyndactyly involving duplication and fusion of digits on the medial side of the foot or hand
Congenital presentation of limb anomalies apparent at birth
Lack of associated systemic malformations or syndromic features

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of hallux varus deformity and preaxial polysyndactyly at birth
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical based on limb malformations; genetic testing may assist but is not definitive.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Medial deviation of the great toe (hallux varus)
searchTerms: great toe bent toward middle foot

pathognomonic.symptomName: Preaxial polysyndactyly with duplication of first digit

common.symptomName: Limited range of motion in affected toes

searchTerms: abnormal gait due to foot shape
difficulty walking caused by foot issues

common.symptomName: Mild soft tissue contractures around affected digits
searchTerms: mild tightening of soft tissues around fingers or toes
limited soft tissue flexibility in digits

common.symptomName: Unilateral or bilateral involvement of feet
searchTerms: foot deformities on one or both sides

common.symptomName: Associated preaxial polydactyly of the hand (less frequent)
searchTerms: extra fingers on hand's thumb side

occasional.symptomName: Mild foot pain secondary to deformity
searchTerms: aching feet related to foot problems

occasional.symptomName: Callus formation on medial foot due to abnormal pressure
searchTerms: calluses on inner foot from pressure
one limb shorter than the other
nail deformities on duplicated fingers or toes
unusual nail growth on extra digits
joint wear and tear in affected areas
degenerative joint disease in affected limbs
nerve and blood flow problems in limb
reduced circulation and sensation in affected limb

rare.symptomName: Associated mild developmental delay (uncommon but reported)

imaging: Radiographs showing medial deviation of the great toe
X-ray evidence of preaxial polydactyly with duplicated metatarsals or phalanges
genetic: Possible mutations in genes regulating limb development (e.g., GLI3, ZRS enhancer region) though no definitive gene identified
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic limb malformations

distinguishingFeatures: Lateral deviation of the great toe (hallux valgus) instead of medial

redFlags: Severe limb deformity causing functional impairment
Presence of systemic malformations suggesting syndromic diagnosis
references: Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man (OMIM) - Limb Malformations
Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation, 7th Edition
